item.content: {"url": "https://api.crossref.org/works?query=mechanical+enforcement+of+state+persistence+in+autonomous+agent+reasoning&rows=4&select=DOI%2Ctitle%2Cabstract%2CURL%2Cpublished", "scope": "Crossref bibliographic metadata and abstracts where supplied; not full papers", "excerpt": "[{\"DOI\": \"10.2139/ssrn.6520840\", \"title\": [\"Agent Safety Alignment and Policy Enforcement for Azure Based Autonomous Agents\"], \"abstract\": \"<jats:p>Increasingly, autonomous actors in the cloud can carry out important decision-making, infrastructure administration, and enterprise automation functions, generating an immediate demand on the safety correspondence and policy. Cloud equipped with Microsoft Azure cloud has scalable orchestration, identity governance, and AI infrastructure are features that support autonomous agents but also pose complex governance and security threats (Bellamkonda et al.; Lakkarasu). This paper designs and analyzes a policy spec ,fiction of an autonomous agent safety architecture on Azure that enables identity control, behavioral tracing, automatic policy, and secure orchestration pipelines (Carcagni; Turetken). The study adopts a joint experimental and architectural assessment approach through simulated agent workflows, enforcement rules and anomaly detector mechanisms deployed in the Azure Kubernetes service, Azure Policy and Azure API management (Carcagni; Sailakshmi). The findings demonstrate that there are quantifiable increases in policy adherence, decreases in unauthorized agent behaviours and greater transparency in autonomous decision-making (Tutuncuoglu; Ardebili and Bartolini). Surprising results provide insights into the risks of misalignment, which is due to the latency of orchestration, vulnerability to identity reuse and the failure of policies to propagate across distributed subsystems (Interrante Bonadia; Nyamboga). These results reveal the vulnerabilities in the structure of the current models of cloud governance. The paper concludes that governance based on the integration of safety, constant monitoring, and policy pipelines as practical guidelines that can be enforced in the context of Azure architecture is a key to successful safety alignment and the possibility of deploying autonomous agents safely in both enterprise, healthcare, and industrial contexts (Asante; Badoi et al.).</jats:p>\", \"URL\": \"https://doi.org/10.2139/ss…
